clinical_scope.population: Adults in acute care, emergency department, ward deterioration, ICU, ambulance or immediate prehospital settings. Use local definitions for adult age threshold; NICE NG253 covers people aged 16 or over.
excluded_populations: Pregnant or recently pregnant patients unless a dedicated obstetric sepsis pathway is used
clinical_scope.intended_use: High-risk candidate retrieval and guideline-based verification for suspected Septic Shock.
clinical_scope.important_boundary: This graph supports clinical reasoning and missed-diagnosis risk reduction; it is not an autonomous diagnostic system.

distinctions.description: Septic shock is a high-mortality subset of sepsis characterized by profound circulatory, cellular, and metabolic abnormalities.

basic_info.working_definition: Septic shock is a subset of sepsis in which underlying circulatory, cellular, and metabolic abnormalities are sufficiently profound to substantially increase mortality.
why_high_risk_for_missed_diagnosis: Septic shock may evolve rapidly from infection or sepsis before all laboratory or resuscitation data are available.
Hypotension, hypoperfusion, altered mental status, oliguria, or elevated lactate may be attributed to noninfectious shock states unless infection is actively considered.
Vasopressor requirement, adequate fluid status, and lactate may be missing or pending early in evaluation.
Delayed recognition can postpone resuscitation, antimicrobial pathway activation, source control assessment, ICU escalation, and organ support.
basic_info.time_sensitivity: Immediately life-threatening; suspected septic shock requires urgent recognition of infection with shock physiology, lactate/perfusion assessment, resuscitation status review, vasopressor/ICU escalation assessment, and source-control evaluation.
do_not_use_as: Pediatric, neonatal, obstetric, or postpartum-specific pathways
Replacing local antimicrobial, vasopressor, ICU, or resuscitation protocols

activation_logic.value: Trigger septic shock graph expansion when a case contains infection context plus shock, hypoperfusion, organ dysfunction, or critical care treatment clues.

value.rationale: Infection plus hypotension is a major shock-pattern trigger; septic shock cannot be confirmed without fluid response, vasopressor requirement, and lactate context.
Vasopressor requirement in an infected patient is a core septic shock signal; verify MAP target, fluid status, and lactate.
Elevated lactate with infection and shock/hypoperfusion should trigger immediate septic shock pathway verification.
This pattern can indicate severe infection with shock physiology even before labs are available.
Renal dysfunction plus shock physiology supports sepsis severity and requires shock verification.

value.logic: infection_context AND tachycardia AND tachypnea AND systemic_symptoms
value.rationale: May represent sepsis; expand sepsis graph first and septic shock graph if hypotension, lactate, or vasopressor information appears.
Unknown source does not exclude septic shock; differential shock etiologies must be evaluated.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Does the case contain suspected or confirmed infection, antimicrobial indication, positive cultures, fever/hypothermia with source symptoms, or clinician concern for infection?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Proceed to sepsis and shock physiology verification.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Do not confirm septic shock; continue shock differential and report infection evidence as absent or not_provided.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Mark infection context as not_provided; septic shock cannot be classified as confirmed without plausible infection.

guideline_verification_pathway.step_name: Identify acute organ dysfunction / sepsis physiology
guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is there acute organ dysfunction or physiologic deterioration compatible with sepsis?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Supports parent sepsis context and justifies shock verification.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Lower certainty; do not exclude if data are missing or shock physiology is present.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: List missing organ dysfunction data and continue if hypotension, vasopressor use, or lactate elevation is present.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is there hypotension, persistent hypotension, MAP below target, signs of hypoperfusion, collapse/syncope, altered mentation, mottling, cyanosis, or oliguria?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Classify as shock physiology; prioritize septic shock if infection context is present.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Septic shock is less supported, but sepsis without shock may still be possible.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Report lack of hemodynamic data as critical missing information.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Has adequate IV fluid resuscitation been given or is there a documented reason to individualize/limit fluids?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: If hypotension persists, proceed to vasopressor and lactate criteria.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If not resuscitated and no contraindication, classify as possible/probable septic shock pending resuscitation response rather than confirmed Sepsis-3 septic shock.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Mark adequate_fluid_status as unknown; core septic shock criteria cannot be fully verified.

guideline_verification_pathway.step_name: Verify vasopressor requirement and MAP target
guideline_verification_pathway.check: Does the patient require vasopressor therapy to maintain MAP at or around 65 mm Hg after adequate fluid resuscitation / without hypovolemia?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Meets vasopressor component of septic shock criteria.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If no vasopressors are required and MAP is adequate after fluids, confirmed septic shock is not supported; consider sepsis with hypoperfusion or another state.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Report vasopressor requirement and MAP as critical missing information.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is lactate >2 mmol/L despite adequate volume resuscitation, and are serial lactates available if initially elevated?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Meets metabolic component of septic shock criteria if infection and vasopressor criteria are also met.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: A lactate <=2 after adequate resuscitation makes Sepsis-3 septic shock less supported, but unstable patients still require clinical evaluation.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Report lactate as critical missing information; do not confirm or exclude septic shock solely from missing lactate.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Were blood cultures collected as soon as possible and ideally before antimicrobials, and were antimicrobials started immediately, ideally within 1 hour of septic shock recognition?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Management aligns with septic shock pathway.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Flag deviation or missing timing; do not delay life-saving antimicrobials solely for cultures.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Report microbiology and antimicrobial timing as missing management verification data.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is a likely infection source identified, and if source control is needed, is early source control planned or performed?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Flag unresolved source; unknown source does not exclude septic shock.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Report source evaluation and source control status as missing critical information.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: If vasopressors are used, is norepinephrine the first-line agent or is there a documented reason for another agent; if norepinephrine is escalating, is vasopressin considered?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Hemodynamic management aligns with septic shock pathway.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Flag mismatch with guideline preference or missing rationale; local protocol and clinician judgment apply.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Report agent and dose trend as missing management verification data.

guideline_verification_pathway.step_name: Check adjunctive and supportive care triggers
guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are there triggers for ICU admission, corticosteroids, inotropes, ventilation/oxygen support, renal support, glucose control, or VTE prophylaxis?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: No additional trigger found in provided data.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Report missing supportive care variables without making unsupported treatment claims.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are there findings suggesting hypovolemic, cardiogenic, obstructive, anaphylactic, adrenal, metabolic, or toxicologic shock instead of or in addition to septic shock?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Report competing or coexisting shock etiologies and do not over-attribute shock to infection.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Septic shock remains favored if infection plus core shock criteria are present.

differential_diagnosis.why_confused: Both can present with hypotension, tachycardia, elevated lactate, cool extremities, and altered mentation.
distinguishing_features: bleeding, dehydration, gastrointestinal fluid loss, burns, diuretic excess
absence of infection signs does not fully exclude infection but lowers septic shock support

differential_diagnosis.why_confused: Can cause hypotension, hypoperfusion, elevated lactate, pulmonary edema, and altered mentation.
Massive PE, tamponade, or tension pneumothorax can mimic septic shock and require different immediate treatment.
distinguishing_features: unilateral absent breath sounds or tension pneumothorax signs

differential_diagnosis.why_confused: Can cause distributive shock with hypotension and respiratory symptoms.
Can produce refractory hypotension and can be precipitated by infection.
DKA can cause dehydration, tachycardia, hypotension, acidosis, and altered mental status; infection can trigger DKA and sepsis.
Drug toxicity can cause hypotension, altered mental status, acidosis, or bradycardia/tachycardia.

next_verification_actions: Obtain/confirm lactate and repeat if elevated
Document MAP, fluid response, and vasopressor requirement
Confirm suspected infection source and cultures

evidence_sources.title: The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3)
evidence_sources.summary: Defines septic shock as a subset of sepsis with profound circulatory/cellular/metabolic abnormalities and clinical identification by vasopressor requirement for MAP >=65 mm Hg plus lactate >2 mmol/L after adequate fluid resuscitation / in absence of hypovolemia.

evidence_sources.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
evidence_sources.publisher: Society of Critical Care Medicine / Surviving Sepsis Campaign
evidence_sources.summary: Recommends blood cultures as soon as possible and ideally before antimicrobials; suggests measuring lactate in adults with possible, probable, or definite sepsis or septic shock.

evidence_sources.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
evidence_sources.publisher: Society of Critical Care Medicine / Surviving Sepsis Campaign
evidence_sources.summary: States that sepsis and septic shock are medical emergencies; suggests at least 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid in the first 3 hours for sepsis-induced hypoperfusion or septic shock; suggests fluid bolus followed by vasopressor support if hypotension persists, with concurrent vasopressors and fluids warranted in unstable shock case-by-case.

evidence_sources.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
evidence_sources.publisher: Society of Critical Care Medicine / Surviving Sepsis Campaign
evidence_sources.summary: Suggests starting vasopressors peripherally rather than delaying for central access when needed; recommends initial MAP target of 65 mm Hg; recommends immediate antimicrobial therapy ideally within 1 hour for septic shock; suggests ICU admission within 6 hours for sepsis or septic shock requiring ICU admission.

evidence_sources.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
evidence_sources.publisher: Society of Critical Care Medicine / Surviving Sepsis Campaign
evidence_sources.summary: Recommends rapid evaluation for anatomical source control; suggests early source control ideally within 6 hours when required; provides antimicrobial stewardship recommendations including MDR risk coverage and de-escalation; suggests clinical evaluation alone over procalcitonin plus clinical evaluation to decide whether to start antimicrobials.

evidence_sources.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
evidence_sources.publisher: Society of Critical Care Medicine / Surviving Sepsis Campaign
evidence_sources.summary: Suggests serial lactate measurements to guide resuscitation in sepsis with elevated lactate or septic shock, and using capillary refill time as an adjunct to other perfusion measures.

evidence_sources.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
evidence_sources.publisher: Society of Critical Care Medicine / Surviving Sepsis Campaign
evidence_sources.summary: Recommends norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor for adults with septic shock; suggests adding vasopressin when norepinephrine doses escalate.

evidence_sources.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
evidence_sources.publisher: Society of Critical Care Medicine / Surviving Sepsis Campaign
evidence_sources.summary: Suggests IV corticosteroids for adults with septic shock and contains supportive care recommendations relevant to respiratory support, renal replacement, glucose control, VTE prophylaxis, and avoiding selected adjunctive therapies.

evidence_sources.title: Suspected sepsis in people aged 16 or over: recognition, assessment and early management (NG253)
evidence_sources.summary: For high-risk adults, NICE recommends urgent assessment, blood gas including glucose and lactate, blood culture, FBC, CRP, urea/electrolytes, broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour of NEWS2 calculation, and prompt IV fluid bolus when high risk unless contraindicated; moderate risk with hypoperfusion should be treated as high risk.

evidence_sources.title: Internal safety rules for single-pass septic shock decision support
evidence_sources.summary: Do not ask follow-up questions in single-pass mode; report missing critical information, avoid overdiagnosis, and explicitly evaluate competing shock etiologies.

must_not: Do not output a confirmed septic shock classification unless infection/sepsis context, vasopressor requirement for MAP target after adequate fluids/no hypovolemia, and lactate >2 mmol/L after resuscitation are documented.
Do not rule out septic shock solely because fever is absent; hypothermia or normothermia may occur in severe infection.
Do not rule out septic shock solely because the infection source is unknown on first assessment.
Do not use lactate alone to diagnose septic shock; lactate elevation must be interpreted with clinical context and other causes of lactate elevation.
Do not delay emergency treatment recommendations in the output just because cultures are missing; mark cultures as ideally before antimicrobials but not a reason to delay life-saving therapy.
Do not select, dose, or prescribe vasopressors, antimicrobials, corticosteroids, or fluids beyond guideline-level pathway statements; local protocol and clinician judgment are required.

Always report missing critical data: MAP/SBP, lactate, fluid response, vasopressor requirement, infection source, antimicrobial timing, cultures, oxygenation, urine output, mental status, and competing shock etiologies.
Always consider noninfectious shock etiologies and coexistence, especially cardiogenic, hypovolemic, obstructive, anaphylactic, adrenal crisis, DKA, toxicologic shock.
safety_constraints.final_output_disclaimer: This knowledge graph is for clinical decision support and missed-diagnosis risk analysis. It does not provide a standalone diagnosis or replace emergency care, clinician assessment, local protocols, or specialist consultation.
